description.narrative:
1. Federation of Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries supported over 30 MSMEs in supply chain of Amazon to adopt responsible management practices and COVID-19 preventive measures applying SCORE and guided Amazon sustainability division to raise awareness on gender and labour rights (in particular, wages, working time, grievance mechanism and dialogue) among the suppliers, besides establishing monitoring mechanisms.
2. Draft national action plan on business and human rights developed in consultation with Stakeholders by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs in line with the UN guiding principles on Business and Human Rights.
3. Ministry of MSME applied SCORE short training tool to guide MSMEs in safe resumption of business post-COVID-19 lockdown in 2020, alongside respecting the rights of workers. 4. Lead brands alongwith Apparel Export Promotion Council agreed on measures to protect rights of workers in the supply chain, with particulr focus on wage and job cuts,especially due to impact on suppliers as a result of cancellation of orders. 1. Technical guidance provided to the SCORE trainers engaged by FICCI in delivering SCORE training to over 30 MSMEs suppliers of Amazon, including guide them on COVID-19 preventive measures and business continuity to prevent incidence of compromises in working conditions and violation of rights of workers in workplace, due to COVID-19. 2. Over 120 suppliers of H&M advised on OSH and COVID-19 preventive measures, grievance redressal and workplace cooperation and demonstrated practical adoption applying SCORE training tool 3. Technical note submitted to Ministry of Corporate Affairs on reflecting decent work elements and capturing the voice of constituents in the draft Nation action plan 4. MNE declaration and other ILO tools promoted in South Asia Business and Human rights forum organized jointly by ILO and UNDP 5. Technical inputs provided to Ministry of MSME in applying SCORE short course in their Entrepreneurship Skill Development Scheme towards guiding MSMEs to resume operations without compromising on the working conditions

description.narrative: 1.Online MSME registration portal, “Udyam’ launched by Ministry of MSME in November 2020 to reduce documentation burden and incentivize MSMEs to register and access government schemes. 2. Uttar Pradesh state labour Department is operationalising a roadmap promoting transition to formality of informal and home based enterprises and workers. Nodal officials have initiated convergence of social protection and other schemes for informal economy workers, in 3 districts offered by various departments to streamline access and expand coverage. 3. The Uttar Pradesh (UP) unorganized workers social security welfare board has reactivated its operations in the aftermath of impact of COVID-19 on informal economy workers and has conceptualised a model for identification and enrolment of home based workers in the welfare board. 4.OSH training roll out including a handbook and posters by State labour department in UP and TN, have benefitted over 300 small, informal and home based enterprises. Central trade unions, AITUC in UP and TN and SEWA in UP and Delhi have trained over 10, 200 informal and home based workers (6280 women) on improving health & safety, wages and gender rights using ILO tools. 5. Tirrupur Exporters Association supported micro enterprises to organize and register with them. It has piloted with over 20 units to set-up gender and OSH committees. 6. The wage rules for new wage code which came into effect in July 2020 aligns piece rate and time rated wages with notified minimum wages, following advocacy and evidence-based inputs by trade unions in policy discussions. This has paved the way for fair remuneration to home-based workers who mostly work on piece-rate basis. 7. The AIOE- FICCI MSME helpdesk services supported more than 40 MSMEs to avail policy measures, in particular, related to COVID-19 and also sustain business, besides guiding 20 micro units to register in its first 6 months of operation. 1.ILO policy note on implication of new MSME definition on generation of employment and its quality by MSMEs in India contributed to the enhanced understanding by policy makers of the correlation of MSME definition, linked policy incentives and its implication on informality, job creation and labour law coverage. 2. Analysis of policy environment, incl. practices of constituents in one state (Odisha) applying EESE tool, guided the development of a tripartite action plan to facilitate formalization of enterprises. 3. Technical guidance provided to All India Organisation of Employers (AIOE) and Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industries (FICCI) to jointly establish a MSME helpdesk with the aim 1) to support informal enterprises to register and avail policy measures, especially to counter COVID- 19 impact, 2) to advocate with its corporate members theregistration of units in the supply chain and registration of workers, 3) to provide business continuity support and guidance on labour management to MSMEs at risk of informality to prevent compromises in working conditions and business closure 3. More than 150 officials from labour and MSME department and factory inspectors in two states (UP and TN) were trained as OSH trainers by ILO, including on COVID-19 prevention in workplace using WISH. A local adapted WISH handbook for home-based workers was produced which also includes section on COVID-19 prevention 4. ILO capacity building workshops with constituents on wage determination, in particular with trade unions strengthened understanding on piece-rate wages. Technical support provided to trade unions to submit evidence-based position on inclusion of piece-rate wages in the new Wage code. 5. SIYB on-line short orientation cum training provided to partners of UNHCR, 55 officials from 10 states, 25 representatives of central trade unions to guide and coach the informal workers impacted due to COVID-19 on espousing the path of self-employment.

description.narrative: 1.Trade unions, Self Employed Women Association in Uttar Pradesh (UP) & Delhi, All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) in UP and Tamil Nadu have unionized 20,205 home based workers out of which 17,211 are women. The unions are offering innovative and localised services including knowledge building on piece-rate calculation and negotiation of better rates with contractors jointly as a collective. 2. A new dedicated union for home based workers has been established by All India Trade Union Congress and registration was approved by the State Labour Department of Uttar Pradesh. The formation of the union is a significant step in addressing and making HBW visible who have been traditionally dependent on contractors 3. State Labour Department has agreed to cover homebased workers in the garment sector in the collective bargaining agreements in Tirrupur district following advocacy efforts by TUs. 1. Technical guidance provided to trade unions on designing and adopting new membership strategies to expand outreach to home-based and informal workers and enterprises, including support in organizing and registering a new dedicated union for home based workers. 2. Advise provided to trade unions on guiding home-based workers in collectively negotiate with contractors to receive orders and demand better rates based on the ILO training on wage determination. 3. The national working group on home based and informal workers set up with the support of the Government of Japan has been guided by ILO in consolidating trade union position on the new labour codes by reviewing them from the perspective of informal workers.
